files.name: MultipartParser.java

notes.4: Attempts to parse the multipart upload.
notes.5: If parsing fails (which the attacker can force), handle the error.
notes.6: Reads the request's Content-Type header — attacker-controlled.
notes.8: Builds a localized error message that includes the Content-Type as a parameter.
notes.11: Adds the error. The message text is run through OGNL expression evaluation.

options.label: `parseRequest` buffers the whole upload in memory, enabling a DoS
options.whyWrong: Memory use isn't the issue; the error-handling path evaluates attacker input as code.

options.label: The attacker-controlled Content-Type is placed into a message that `findText` evaluates as an OGNL expression, so a `%{...}` payload runs Java code
`getContentType()` may return null and cause a NullPointerException
options.whyWrong: A possible NPE is a crash, not the remote code execution this creates.

options.label: Strip '%{' and '${' from the Content-Type
options.whyWrong: Nested/obfuscated expressions can reconstruct the markers after naive stripping.

options.label: Do not pass user-controlled text through OGNL; build the error message without expression evaluation
Return HTTP 400 when parsing fails
options.whyWrong: The OGNL has already been evaluated while building `msg`, before any response status is set.

training.exploit: Send a request whose `Content-Type` header is a malformed multipart value containing an OGNL payload, e.g. `%{(#cmd='id').(#execute=@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec(#cmd))...}`. Parsing fails, the error builder runs the Content-Type through `findText`/OGNL, and the embedded expression executes the command — unauthenticated RCE. (This was the Equifax-breach bug.)

hints.line: The RCE happens while constructing the error message.
hints.bugClass: Attacker text is evaluated as an expression language.
hints.why: What does findText do with `%{...}` in the text?
hints.fix: Never evaluate user-controlled strings as OGNL.

writeup.summary: When multipart parsing failed, Struts built a localized error message that embedded the raw `Content-Type` header and then evaluated that message as an OGNL expression. An attacker sent a `Content-Type` containing a `%{...}` payload; forcing a parse error made Struts evaluate it, executing arbitrary Java — unauthenticated remote code execution (the 2017 bug behind the Equifax breach). The real fix stopped evaluating user-controlled error text as OGNL; stripping expression markers was bypassable.
